mainTopic: The מחלוקת of רב and שמואל about a condition made at קידושין but not repeated at נישואין, and רבה's limits on that argument, tested by אביי's challenges.
overview: The גמרא continues the מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about a man who made קידושין on condition that she has no נדרים and then married her without repeating the condition. It pushes away a proof against שמואל, and then reads the משנה so that it actually supports him. It then asks why, in a plain case with no condition at all, she loses her כתובה but still needs a גט. רבה and רב חסדא answer that the גט is only rabbinic. רבא answers that the תנא is in doubt, so he is lenient on money and strict on איסור. רבה then limits the argument of רב and שמואל. After אביי challenges him, רבה's statement is reworded: they argue only about one woman married twice, like two women, but in a plain one-woman mistake everyone agrees no גט is needed. אביי attacks this with a ברייתא about קידושין with less than a פרוטה and a ברייתא about 'on condition that my father agrees,' and the גמרא answers both. Finally אביי brings a ברייתא about a young girl who was divorced and taken back, and the challenge from it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The proof is pushed away: no condition at either stage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's 'leaves without כתובה' case is where he did both קידושין and נישואין with no condition at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case is where he betrothed her without any condition and married her without any condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the earlier proof against שמואל. It says the משנה that requires a גט is not talking about a conditional קידושין at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof assumed the משנה's case was 'conditional קידושין, plain נישואין.' Now the גמרא says it is 'plain קידושין, plain נישואין.' A case like that tells us nothing about שמואל's case, so the proof against him falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: He betrothed her (the stage of קידושין)
Without specifying, with no condition stated
He married her, brought her into the home (נישואין)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate stages here: קידושין (betrothal) and נישואין (marriage). A condition can be said at one stage and not repeated at the other. That is the whole question.

phrases.english: No, he betrothed her without specification,
and married her without specification.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, קִידְּשָׁה סְתָם, וּכְנָסָהּ סְתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof against שמואל that came just before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the identification of the משנה's case as conditional קידושין followed by plain נישואין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the wrong case. The משנה can be read as having no condition at any stage.

steps.title: Then the משנה should have taught the bigger חידוש
steps.stepSummary: If conditional קידושין followed by plain נישואין really needs no גט, the משנה should have taught that stronger case instead of the simple one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he betrothed her with a condition and married her plainly, is it true that she needs no גט? If so, instead of teaching 'one who betroths a woman on condition that she has no vows, and vows are found, she is not betrothed,' let it teach: 'he married her plainly and vows were found, she is not betrothed,' and all the more so this case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading. If שמואל is right, the משנה chose to teach the weaker case when it could have taught the stronger one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the condition still works even when he married her without repeating it. Then that case is the bigger news. The simple case of only a conditional קידושין would follow from it with a קל וחומר. A משנה usually teaches the stronger case, so why did it leave that case out?

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל, קִידְּשָׁה עַל תְּנַאי וּכְנָסָהּ סְתָם —
phrases.english: But if he betrothed her with a condition and married her without specification,
is it indeed so that she does not need a bill of divorce?
Instead of teaching: one who betroths a woman
on condition that there are no vows on her
and vows were found on her, she is not betrothed,
let it teach: he married her without specification
phrases.notes: He means after a conditional קידושין.

phrases.english: and vows were found on her, she is not betrothed,
and all the more so this case.
phrases.notes: 'This case' is the plain case the משנה actually teaches, with only a conditional קידושין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל, קִידְּשָׁה עַל תְּנַאי וּכְנָסָהּ סְתָם — הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא בָּעֲיָא גִּיטָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of the משנה offered in step 1, since that reading leaves שמואל's case untaught.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of שמואל, together with the reading of the משנה in step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should teach the bigger חידוש. If plain נישואין after conditional קידושין still voids the marriage, that is the stronger case and should have been taught.

steps.title: Reading the משנה so it does teach that case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה does mean the stronger case. It is read as: conditional קידושין plus plain נישואין means she is not betrothed, while plain קידושין plus plain נישואין means she leaves without a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what it is saying: one who betroths a woman on condition that she has no vows, and then marries her plainly, and vows are found, she is not betrothed. If he betrothed her plainly and married her plainly, she leaves without a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה really is teaching שמואל's case, and its two halves are read as two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the משנה is now read to include 'and he married her plainly.' That gives the bigger חידוש the challenge asked for. The second half ('leaves without a כתובה') is the case where there was no condition at any stage.

keyTerms.meaning: That is indeed what it is saying

steps.whatToRemember: According to this reading, the משנה supports שמואל: a condition made at קידושין still works even if he married her without repeating it. With no condition at all, she only loses her כתובה.

phrases.english: That is also what it is saying:
One who betroths a woman on condition
that there are no vows on her, and married her without specification,
and vows were found on her, she is not betrothed.
If he betrothed her without specification and married her without specification,
she leaves without a marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by reading the stronger case into the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's first half is only about a conditional קידושין, so it leaves out the stronger case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first half includes 'and he married her plainly.' The 'leaves without a כתובה' half refers to no condition at any stage.

steps.title: If he can say 'I don't want a vower,' why does she need a גט?
steps.stepSummary: From 'without a כתובה' we learn she still needs a גט. But if she loses the כתובה because he does not want a wife who makes נדרים, the marriage should be a mistake, and no גט should be needed either.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only the כתובה she does not get, which means she does need a גט. And why does she not get the כתובה? Because he says, 'I do not want a wife who makes vows.' If so, she should not need a גט either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to the ruling just read into the משנה. If the husband's claim takes away her כתובה, why does it not cancel the marriage completely?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only that she loses the כתובה, so she must still need a גט. But the reason she loses the כתובה is that the husband clearly objects to such a wife. That sounds like a mistaken transaction (מקח טעות), which should cancel the קידושין itself. The next two steps give two answers.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who habitually makes vows

steps.confusionAlert: Losing the כתובה and not needing a גט are two different results. The גמרא's question is why the husband's objection is strong enough for the first result but not for the second.

phrases.english: It is the marriage contract that she does not get,
but a bill of divorce she does need.
And why is it that she does not get the marriage contract?
Because he says: I do not want a wife who makes vows,

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי גֵּט נָמֵי לָא תִּיבְּעֵי!
phrases.english: if so, she should not need a bill of divorce either!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתוּבָּה הוּא דְּלָא בָּעֲיָא, הָא גִּיטָּא — בָּעֲיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the second half of the משנה as read in step 3 and questions why it requires a גט.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that plain קידושין and plain נישואין means she leaves without a כתובה but still needs a גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason given for losing the כתובה (he does not want a wife who makes נדרים) would also make the marriage a mistake. Then no גט should be needed.

steps.title: The גט is only required by the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב חסדא answer that by תורה law she needs no גט, but the Rabbis require one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: She needs a גט only by rabbinic law. And רב חסדא said the same: She needs a גט only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4. רבה and רב חסדא say the גט is only a rabbinic requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 asked: if the marriage is a mistake, why does she need a גט? The answer is that by תורה law she really does not need one. The Rabbis still require a גט because he never stated the condition out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: From their words, meaning by rabbinic law and not by תורה law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the marriage is fully valid by תורה law. The point is the opposite: by תורה law she needs no גט, and the requirement comes only from the Rabbis.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
She needs a bill of divorce by their words.
phrases.notes: "Their words" means the Rabbis. By תורה law she would not need a גט.

phrases.english: And so too Rav Chisda said:
She needs a bill of divorce by their words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: צְרִיכָה גֵּט מִדִּבְרֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the levels of law: no גט by תורה law, but a גט by rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the marriage is a mistake, so that she loses her כתובה, she should not need a גט either
steps.terutzMaskana: The marriage is a mistake by תורה law. The גט is only a rabbinic stringency.

steps.title: The תנא is unsure, so he is lenient on money and strict on איסור
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer: the תנא is in doubt whether the marriage is valid, so each side of the case follows the rules of doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The תנא is unsure about this case. With money, we go lenient. With prohibitions, we go strict.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the question from Step 4. The תנא is not sure the marriage is valid, so he handles money and איסור differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because of the doubt, the woman cannot take the money of a כתובה from the husband. Someone who wants to take money must prove their claim. But for איסור matters such as אשת איש we must be strict, so she needs a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: He is in doubt about it
In money matters, we go lenient
In prohibition matters, we go strict

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic rule for handling a ספק: the same doubt can lead to a lenient result in money and a strict result in איסור.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers: רבה and רב חסדא say the גט is rabbinic. רבא says the doubt makes us lenient on the כתובה and strict on the גט.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The tanna is in doubt about it,
regarding money, to be lenient,
phrases.notes: Lenient for the husband: she cannot collect the כתובה.

phrases.english: regarding prohibition, to be strict.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: תַּנָּא סַפּוֹקֵי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question that Step 5 answered
steps.terutzResolutionType: Doubt handled with two different rules: lenient for money, strict for איסור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Losing the כתובה and needing a גט seem to contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Both come from one doubt, applied by different rules

steps.title: רבה limits the argument of רב and שמואל to two women
steps.stepSummary: רבה says רב and שמואל only argue when the mistake involves two women. With one woman, everyone agrees no גט is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The argument is about a mistake with two women. But with a mistake about one woman, everyone agrees she does not need a גט from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה makes a new statement about where רב and שמואל disagree. He says their argument is only about a case with two women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the two-women case, a man married one woman on condition that she has no נדרים, and then married a second woman with no condition. The question is whether his condition with the first woman shows he cares about it with the second too. With one woman married on a condition, even רב agrees no גט is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The argument, here between רב and שמואל
A mistake, here a marriage based on a false assumption

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The argument is in a mistake of two women.
phrases.notes: He means the argument between רב and שמואל: one wife married with a condition, a second wife married without one.

phrases.english: But in a mistake of one woman,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט.
phrases.english: all agree she does not need a bill of divorce from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּטָעוּת שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the משנה to defining the scope of the argument between רב and שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב and שמואל argue only about two women. With one woman, everyone agrees no גט is needed.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה is about one woman
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: the משנה talks about one woman, and we used it to challenge שמואל, so the argument must include the one-woman case.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But the משנה is about a mistake with one woman, and we raised a challenge from it against שמואל!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's statement from Step 7. The משנה has only one woman, yet the גמרא used it in the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא used the משנה to challenge שמואל, as if the משנה supports רב. That only makes sense if רב and שמואל argue in a one-woman case. So רבה cannot say everyone agrees about one woman.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, used to point out a problem

phrases.english: Abaye said (to him):
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, אביי is speaking to רבה.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּטָעוּת אִשָּׁה אַחַת הִיא,
phrases.english: But the Mishnah is a mistake of one woman,
and we raise a challenge from it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּטָעוּת אִשָּׁה אַחַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement of רבה in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that everyone agrees in a one-woman case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה is a one-woman case and was used against שמואל, so there must be an argument even about one woman

steps.title: רבה's statement is reworded: one woman that is like two women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רבה's statement: the argument is about one woman in a case like two women, but in a simple one-woman case everyone agrees no גט is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said. רבה said: The argument is about a mistake with one woman that is like two women. But with a plain mistake about one woman alone, everyone agrees she does not need a גט from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes back the first version of רבה's statement and gives a corrected version. The argument is about one woman in a case that looks like two women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a man who married a woman on a condition, divorced her, and then married her again with no condition. That one woman is like two separate marriages, and רב and שמואל argue whether the old condition still applies. In a simple case of one woman married on a condition, everyone agrees there is no גט.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said, a formula for correcting a quoted statement

steps.whatToRemember: Final version of רבה: רב and שמואל argue about one woman who was married twice, like two women. In a plain one-woman case, everyone agrees no גט is needed.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
Rabba said:
The argument is in a mistake of one woman
that is like two women.
phrases.notes: For example, he married her on a condition, divorced her, then married her again with no condition.

phrases.english: But in a mistake of just one woman alone,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט.
phrases.english: all agree she does not need a bill of divorce from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אִתְּמַר הָכִי אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in Step 8 by rewording רבה's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה said the argument was only about two different women
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about one woman in a case like two women, such as a remarriage after divorce. A plain one-woman case needs no גט according to everyone.

steps.title: אביי quotes a ברייתא about mistaken קידושין
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ברייתא: קידושין done in error, with less than a פרוטה, or by a קטן do not take effect even if gifts were sent later. The תנא קמא says relations afterward do acquire her. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: If a man betrothed a woman by mistake, or with less than a פרוטה, or a minor betrothed her, then even if he sent gifts afterward she is not betrothed, because he sent them based on the first betrothal. But if they had relations with her, they acquired her. רבי שמעון בן יהודה said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: even if they had relations, they did not acquire her.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes a ברייתא that he will use to attack רבה. This step sets up the challenge, and the actual point comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three kinds of קידושין that don't work. Gifts sent later don't fix them, because he sent the gifts thinking the first קידושין were real. The two תנאים argue about whether later relations count as new קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Gifts a groom sends his bride
Less than the value of a פרוטה, the smallest amount that works for קידושין
They acquired her, meaning she is married

phrases.english: Abaye challenged him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבה, whose reworded rule we just saw.

phrases.english: If he betrothed her by mistake,
or with less than a perutah's worth,
and likewise a minor who betrothed,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁלַח סִבְלוֹנוֹת לְאַחַר מִיכֵּן —
phrases.english: even though he sent gifts afterward,
she is not betrothed,
because he sent them on account of the first betrothal.
But if they had relations with her, they acquired her.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
If they had relations, they did not acquire her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to attack רבה's reworded statement in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that in a simple one-woman mistake everyone agrees no גט is needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The setup: a ברייתא shows a dispute about a mistaken קידושין followed by relations.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to be a one-woman mistake about vows
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that the ברייתא's 'mistake' involves one woman and the תנאים argue about it. It seems to be a mistake about נדרים, which contradicts רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here the mistake involves one woman, and they argue! Isn't it a mistake about vows?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes his point. The ברייתא shows an argument in a simple one-woman case, so רבה is wrong to say everyone agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reads 'betrothed by mistake' as the classic case where he thought she had no נדרים and she did. That is a one-woman mistake. Yet the תנא קמא says the relations work as קידושין, so not everyone agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake about her vows: he thought she had none, and she did
Isn't it that... (a leading question that pushes a reading)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא דְּטָעוּת אִשָּׁה אַחַת הִיא,
phrases.english: But here it is a mistake involving one woman,
and they argue.
Isn't it a mistake about vows?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא דְּטָעוּת אִשָּׁה אַחַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the attack based on the ברייתא quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'mistake' means a mistake about נדרים with one woman, and the תנאים argue, then there is a dispute even in the simple one-woman case.

steps.title: The mistake is קידושין with less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's 'mistake' is not about נדרים. It means he gave less than a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is the mistake of less than a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה. The ברייתא's mistake is about the amount given, not about her vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mistake is giving less than a פרוטה, it is not the one-woman case רבה was talking about. So the argument in the ברייתא does not contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: No, the standard way to reject a proposed reading

phrases.english: No, it is the mistake of less than a perutah's worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, טָעוּת פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by redefining the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'mistake' was about her נדרים, a one-woman case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'mistake' is giving less than a פרוטה, so רבה is not contradicted.

steps.title: But less than a פרוטה is listed separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא already mentions less than a פרוטה as its own case. So 'by mistake' must mean something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Less than a פרוטה is taught explicitly: 'If he betrothed her by mistake, or with less than a פרוטה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The ברייתא lists 'by mistake' and 'less than a פרוטה' as two items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'mistake' means less than a פרוטה, the ברייתא would be saying the same thing twice. The wording seems to show these are two different cases.

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי לַהּ:
phrases.english: Less than a perutah's worth is taught explicitly:
"If he betrothed her by mistake, or with less than a perutah's worth"!

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה בְּהֶדְיָא קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'by mistake' means less than a פרוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists both phrases as separate items, so they cannot be the same case.

steps.title: The second phrase explains the first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'less than a פרוטה' is not a new case. It explains what 'by mistake' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is explaining: How did he betroth her by mistake? For example, he betrothed her with less than a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves its answer. It reads the ברייתא so that the second phrase explains the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ו in 'וּפָחוֹת' is read as 'namely' and not 'or'. So the ברייתא has only one case of a mistake, giving less than a פרוטה, and the challenge against רבה falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is explaining, so the second phrase spells out the first

steps.confusionAlert: Don't count three cases in the first part of the ברייתא. According to this answer, 'by mistake' and 'less than a פרוטה' are one case, followed by the קטן case.

phrases.english: It is explaining:
How did he betroth her by mistake?
For example, he betrothed her with less than a perutah's worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרוֹשֵׁי קָא מְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists two separate cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second phrase explains the first, so the only mistake is less than a פרוטה.

steps.title: What is the argument about?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the case is less than a פרוטה, the גמרא asks what the two תנאים are arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they argue?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the argument in the ברייתא. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is now clear: קידושין with less than a פרוטה, and later relations. The גמרא wants to know why one תנא says the relations work as קידושין and the other says they don't.

phrases.english: About what do they argue?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the case is settled, asks for the reasoning of the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic behind the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון בן יהודה.

steps.title: Does a person know less than a פרוטה doesn't work?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that a person knows less than a פרוטה doesn't work, so he has relations to make new קידושין. רבי שמעון בן יהודה holds that he doesn't know, so he has relations relying on the first קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: a person knows that betrothal does not take effect with less than a פרוטה, so he decided to have relations for the sake of betrothal. The other master holds: a person does not know this, so when he has relations, he does so relying on the first betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the argument. It depends on what the man knew when he had relations with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he knows the first קידושין failed, his relations must be meant as new קידושין, so she is married. If he thinks the first קידושין worked, he had no intent to make new קידושין, so nothing happens. The argument is about what a typical person knows. It is not about a one-woman mistake, so רבה's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of making קידושין
With the intention of, relying on

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's argument is about קידושין with less than a פרוטה. The question is whether a person knows that such קידושין don't work. So it is not a one-woman mistake about נדרים, and רבה's rule survives אביי's challenge.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that relations count as קידושין only when the man intends them that way. His intent depends on what he believes about the earlier קידושין.

phrases.english: One master holds:
phrases.notes: This is the תנא קמא, who said the relations do acquire her.

phrases.english: a person knows that betrothal does not take effect
with less than a perutah's worth,
so he decided to have relations for the sake of betrothal.
And the other master holds:
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון בן יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֵין קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין
phrases.english: a person does not know that betrothal does not take effect
with less than a perutah's worth,
and when he has relations,
he has relations relying on the first betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: אָדָם יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֵין קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether a typical person knows that קידושין with less than a פרוטה don't work. That decides whether his later relations were meant as new קידושין.

steps.title: Challenge from the condition 'on condition that my father agrees'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a man makes קידושין through relations on condition that his father agrees. The father does not agree, and the תנא קמא still says she is married, but רבי שמעון בן יהודה disagrees. This looks like a mistake with one woman where the תנאים argue, which goes against the claim that everyone agrees in such a case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: If a man says, 'I am having relations with you for קידושין on condition that my father agrees,' then even though the father did not agree, she is married. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: if the father agreed, she is married; if the father did not agree, she is not married. But here it is like a mistake with one woman, and they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack the earlier rule. Here there is one woman and a flawed condition, and the תנאים still argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said that in a plain one-woman mistake, everyone agrees she is not married and needs no גט. In this ברייתא the condition was not met (the father did not agree), so it looks like a one-woman mistake. Yet the תנא קמא says she is married, so it seems not everyone agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake, a flaw in the קידושין

phrases.english: He challenged him:
'I am having relations with you on condition that my father agrees,'
phrases.notes: He means relations for the sake of קידושין, one of the ways a man can marry a woman.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה הָאָב — מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: even though the father did not agree, she is married.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
if the father agreed, she is married;
if the father did not agree, she is not married.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא, דְּכִי טָעוּת אִשָּׁה אַחַת דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: But here, it is like a mistake with one woman,
and they argue!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: הֲרֵינִי בּוֹעֲלִיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁיִּרְצֶה אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the less-than-a-פרוטה ברייתא, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא to challenge the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reworded rule (step 9) that in a plain one-woman mistake everyone agrees she needs no גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a one-woman case with an unmet condition, yet the תנא קמא rules she is married. So it is not true that everyone agrees she is not married.

steps.title: They argue about what 'my father agrees' means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the argument is not about relations after a mistake. It is about the meaning of the condition: does 'my father agrees' mean he just stays quiet, or that he actually says 'yes'?
steps.simpleTranslation: There, this is what they argue about: One Sage holds that 'on condition that the father agrees' means 'on condition that the father stays quiet,' and he did stay quiet. The other Sage holds it means 'on condition that my father says yes,' and the father did not say yes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The two תנאים are arguing about what the condition means, not about one woman and a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the condition was actually met, because the father stayed quiet, so there was no mistake at all. For רבי שמעון בן יהודה, the condition needed a clear 'yes,' which never came. So the ברייתא has nothing to do with the earlier rule, and the rule still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: 'The father did not agree' in the ברייתא does not mean the father objected. He just did not speak up, and that is exactly what they argue about.

phrases.english: There, this is what they argue about:
One Sage holds that 'on condition that the father agrees'
phrases.notes: This first Sage is the תנא קמא, who said she is married.

phrases.english: means 'on condition that the father stays quiet,'
and he did stay quiet.
And the other Sage holds it means 'on condition that my father says yes,'
and the father did not say yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by changing what the argument is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different question (the meaning of the condition).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנאים argue about whether relations after a failed condition make new קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue only about whether silence counts as agreement. For one Sage the condition was met; for the other it was not.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'father agrees' ברייתא does not disprove the rule. The argument is only about whether a father's silence counts as agreeing.

steps.title: New challenge: the young girl who was divorced and taken back
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: a קטנה married off by her father was divorced, and then her husband took her back while she was still young. If he dies without children, she does חליצה and not יבום, because the divorce was complete but the return was not. The גמרא is setting up a challenge from this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: The חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר about a young girl whose father married her off, and she was divorced, and now she is like an orphan while her father is alive, and her husband took her back. She does חליצה and not יבום, because her divorce was a complete divorce, but her return is not a complete return.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא to challenge the same rule. This step sets up the case, and the ברייתא continues in the next step. The actual attack comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once her father accepted the גט for her, he can no longer marry her off, so the husband takes her back with only her own consent as a קטנה, which is not a full marriage. So while she is still a קטנה, the return is incomplete. The challenge to רבה will come from the next part of the ברייתא, which says what happens once she grows up.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl, under the age of adulthood
An 'orphan' while her father is alive: her father can no longer marry her off
She marries the brother-in-law through יבום

steps.whyThisMatters: This case will test whether a man's relations with his own wife automatically upgrade a weak marriage into a full one.

phrases.english: He challenged him:
The Sages agree with Rabbi Eliezer
about a young girl whose father married her off,
and she was divorced, and she is an orphan in her father's lifetime,
phrases.notes: Once her father has accepted a גט for her, he can no longer marry her off, so she is like an orphan.

phrases.english: and her husband took her back: she does חליצה and not יבום,
because her divorce was a complete divorce,
and her return is not a complete return.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: מוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering the first challenge, the גמרא opens a second challenge from a new ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reworded rule (step 9) that in a plain one-woman mistake everyone agrees she needs no גט, because his later relations rely on the flawed first קידושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step only sets up the case. The attack comes from the next lines (step 20). If she grew up while with him, she becomes a full wife without any new קידושין being mentioned. That implies his relations made a new marriage instead of relying on the weak first one.

steps.title: When the second marriage becomes a full marriage
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the 'חליצה but not יבום' ruling applies only when he divorced her and took her back while she was a קטנה both times. If he took her back after she became a גדולה, or she grew up while married to him, she is a full wife and can do חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this rule apply? When he divorced her while she was a minor and took her back while she was still a minor. But if he divorced her as a minor and took her back as an adult, or took her back as a minor and she grew up while with him, and then he died, she can either do חליצה or יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא from Step 19, which now explains exactly when the ruling applies. The גמרא is setting up its challenge with this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said the return marriage of a קטנה is not complete, so she can only do חליצה. Here the ברייתא adds that if she grew up while living with him, the marriage counts as complete, even though it never mentions new קידושין after she grew up. That detail is what the גמרא will use to challenge the idea from earlier steps about when a man has relations relying on his first קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? A phrase that limits a ruling to a specific case
An adult girl, old enough for her own קידושין to work by תורה law
She grew up while she was with him (while married to him)
He took her back (remarried her after the divorce)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two divorces. Her father married her off, so the first marriage was complete and the divorce works fully. Only the return marriage, which she made herself as a קטנה, is the weak one, and that is what changes once she grows up.

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
When he divorced her while she was a minor
and took her back while she was still a minor.
But if he divorced her while she was a minor
and took her back when she was an adult,
or if he took her back while she was a minor
and she grew up while with him, and he died,
she either does חליצה or does יבום.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים שֶׁגֵּירְשָׁהּ כְּשֶׁהִיא קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא begun in Step 19 by limiting its ruling and adding the case where she grew up while married to him.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view from earlier steps about when a man has relations relying on his earlier קידושין and when he intends new קידושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats a girl who grew up while married to him as a full wife without mentioning new קידושין. The גמרא will use this to test the earlier claims about relations after flawed קידושין.
